headline: The record November patch load settled above 1,300 fixes as agentic penetration-testing frameworks turned up inside live Amazon Web Services breaches and Krebs on Security placed the administrator of Qilin, the world's busiest ransomware affiliate program, in St. Petersburg.

emerging_trends.text: Open-source agentic penetration-testing frameworks keep crossing over into attacker infrastructure, with AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud now tied to Amazon Web Services credential theft three months after ARTEX made the same trip, which means defenders face tooling that reconnoiters, steals keys, and pivots without an operator typing.

Hosting and model-serving platforms have become reservoirs of other companies' secrets, and the bills land on the victims: stolen keys held by Railway produced roughly $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges, while Fireworks AI and NEAR AI lost datasets, model weights, and agent data to single intrusions.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Providers Lose Keys, Datasets, and Model Weights

emerging_trends.text: CISA added Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Webtop to its exploited catalog weeks after fixes existed, and attackers took root on Barracuda gateways patched on November 2, 2026, which puts the real risk in the lag between a vendor's release and a customer's installation.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Barracuda, BroadWorks, and AhsayCBS Under Attack

topics.title: November Patch Tuesday Runs Past Microsoft
topics.latest_developments: Final counts landed above Microsoft's own tally of nearly 1,100: Cisco Talos put the November 2026 release at 1,328 vulnerabilities with 60 critical, 45 of them remote code execution, the SANS Internet Storm Center counted 1,260 with 68 critical and 167 Chromium issues reaching Microsoft Edge, and The Hacker News counted 1,259 fixes including 726 in Windows, 174 in Office, 59 in SQL Server, and 27 in SharePoint Server, and reported that the exploited Outlook bug CVE-2026-124194 may expose NTLMv2 password hashes; Dark Reading told administrators to prioritize that zero-day alongside critical Exchange, SharePoint, Windows Search, and LDAP bugs; Intel and AMD together disclosed more than 200 flaws, among them critical bugs in Intel TDX software and a long run of AMD graphics defects; Adobe fixed 110 across nine products including Experience Manager, Premiere, and Photoshop; Siemens flagged high-severity flaws and Node2Shell exposure alongside pre-Patch Tuesday advisories from VDE CERT, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy; Apple closed Bluetooth and AirPlay pairing flaws, more iMessage bugs, and an exploited Brotli vulnerability; and the same cumulative updates repair the Exchange Server sign-in and mail delivery failures October's Windows Server patches caused plus the USB audio breakage dating to September, with Windows 10 holdouts collecting the month through extended security update KB5131096.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-124194, the Outlook zero-day Microsoft says attackers already exploit, remains the first fix to deploy on Windows estates. Administrators should also pull the Adobe, Intel, AMD, and Apple updates and inventory Siemens, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy equipment before the industrial advisories go stale.

topics.title: Barracuda, BroadWorks, and AhsayCBS Under Attack
topics.latest_developments: Huntress detailed an attack chain from early October 2026 that strings CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS backup software to bypass authentication and run commands, then drops a sandbox-evading Python implant; SecurityWeek confirmed that attackers now bypass authorization and take root on Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances; CISA detailed the two flaws it added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, CVE-2026-20320, an XML external entity bug in Cisco BroadWorks rated 7.5, and CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging's Webtop media transcoder, both of which leak configuration data on patched-but-unupdated systems; SecurityWeek reported that attackers exploiting the critical Xen Orchestra authentication bypass now execute arbitrary code as administrator and take over XCP-ng nodes; and Cynet's CyOps and Research teams watched attackers spend three minutes in October 2026 firing PowerShell reverse shell commands at Qlik Sense servers at several European Union customers, with ActiveMQ and Veeam exploits staged behind them, and the attempts failed.
topics.summary: Every one of these flaws has a fix available, and in each case the lag between release and installation is doing the damage. Operators of Barracuda gateways, Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave Webtop, Xen Orchestra, Qlik Sense, and AhsayCBS should patch now and hunt for post-exploitation activity.

topics.title: AI Providers Lose Keys, Datasets, and Model Weights
topics.latest_developments: Fireworks AI said its inquiry into the incident it first reported October 10, 2026 turned up further malicious activity that reached account and billing information, secrets, datasets, incomplete models, and Notion AI chats for a limited set of accounts; an attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, the open-source inference engine, ran code on a NEAR AI inference server on Sunday, November 8, 2026, took data belonging to 18 agents and roughly 100 users, and could have read requests the server processed that day, confidential-mode requests inside a trusted execution environment included; the security company Claroc counted 37,571 Grok-built applications online, 35,578 of them open to anyone with no sign-in, 24 of them built by staff at X and at SpaceXSI, and about one in ten carrying internal business information or passwords; and Railway promised to cover the roughly $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges itself wherever an AI provider refuses a refund.
topics.summary: Platforms that host applications, agents, and model serving now hold the credentials and artifacts of everyone who builds on them, which turns one intrusion into many. Rotate every AI provider key stored with a third-party platform and audit what hosted applications expose to the open internet.

topics.title: Ten Neurons Backdoor an AI Agent
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Research published a technique it calls Lazarus that implants a hidden backdoor in a capable agent model by editing fewer than ten rarely used neurons, with no retraining; when a chosen trigger appears, the model emits the attacker's command and the agent runs it with the agent's own permissions, and the edited model behaves normally through standard safety evaluations. Microsoft says frontier agents can detect the anomalous weight edits and that it has observed no threat actor using the method; separately, Microsoft's FORGE Lab reported that its MDASH project turned AI-generated Linux kernel findings into 59 upstream bug reports, 33 assigned CVEs, 38 merged fixes, and eight demonstrated local root privilege-escalation exploits.
topics.summary: The attack requires write access to a model's weights, which puts model registries, fine-tuning pipelines, and insiders in the threat path for any organization that grants agents real permissions. Verify provenance and checksums of every model you load, and screen weights for anomalous edits rather than relying on behavioral safety tests.

sources.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons

topics.title: Fortinet, Citrix, and Ivanti Ship Their Own Fixes
topics.latest_developments: Fortinet patched nearly 100 vulnerabilities on November 11, 2026, a volume the company attributes to folding frontier AI models into its product security testing; Citrix and Ivanti closed critical and high-severity flaws that let attackers tamper with certificate entries, run code remotely, and compromise hosts; Zoom fixed two bugs in Zoom Workplace for Windows, among them CVE-2026-108186, an improper input validation flaw rated 9.6 that hands an unauthenticated user an escalation of privilege, and Asus closed bugs enabling command execution and memory overwrites; and the Git project shipped 2.56.1, along with 2.50.2 through 2.55.1, to close six flaws, among them CVE-2026-111760, an integer truncation in Git's index handling that lets a malicious repository run code on any machine that clones it recursively.
topics.summary: Fortinet, Citrix, and Ivanti gear sits at the network edge, which puts their flaws in front of every internet scanner within hours of disclosure. Schedule these appliance updates ahead of the desktop and chipset patches from the same week, and move developer workstations and build runners to the fixed Git releases.

topics.title: AntiFox Agents Steal AWS Credentials
topics.latest_developments: Researchers tied a run of intrusions that stole Amazon Web Services credentials and then pivoted laterally through victim environments to AntiFox, an emerging open-source agentic penetration testing platform that attackers run as self-managed instances on Alibaba Cloud, and linked those hosted AntiFox interfaces to confirmed malicious actions; Dark Reading reported on November 10, 2026 that forks of ARTEX, the framework that made the same jump from published tool to attacker staple, plus 45 similar penetration-testing tools, still run credential attacks and cloud break-ins at machine speed across multiple industries.
topics.summary: AntiFox chains reconnaissance, credential theft, and lateral movement with no operator at the keyboard, which compresses a cloud intrusion into minutes. Retire long-lived AWS access keys in favor of short-lived credentials, and alert on API calls arriving from Alibaba Cloud address ranges.

sources.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets

topics.title: Qilin Unmasked as WhiteArmor Squeezes Maersk
topics.latest_developments: Krebs on Security reported on November 11, 2026 that Qilin has become the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months, and that a decade of operational security mistakes by its administrator all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia; Maersk, the Danish shipping group, confirmed the same day that a threat actor reached a local legacy system the company inherited through an earlier acquisition and pulled data out of it, while the WhiteArmor ransomware crew demands $5 million.
topics.summary: Qilin rents its encryptor and leak site to affiliates who do the breaking in, which is why its victim count outruns every rival program. Companies should hunt for the initial-access routes Qilin affiliates favor, and acquirers should treat inherited legacy systems as unmonitored attack surface until they prove otherwise.

sources.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million

topics.title: Sparrow Malware Ties Three China-Nexus Campaigns
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Research linked three separate threat clusters, one of which it tracks as SilentDelivery, through shared infrastructure and overlapping malware code it groups as the Sparrow ecosystem, and traced a year of operations against telecommunications providers, government organizations, military entities, research institutions, and critical infrastructure in Latin America, Asia, and Europe; Unit 42, the Palo Alto Networks research group, separately detailed Falcon C2, a browser-based threat framework that attacks governments through malicious scripts, browser extensions, and an implant it names Antino.
topics.summary: The shared tooling suggests a common developer or quartermaster supplying several China-nexus espionage teams, which means indicators from one intrusion can surface the others. Telecommunications and government defenders should hunt across all three clusters' infrastructure and extend browser extension inventories to catch Falcon C2's delivery route.

sources.title: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem
The XG Files: Falcon C2 Flying Under The (Browser) Radar

topics.title: N-able Ships Hotfixes for N-central Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: N-able released hotfixes on November 11, 2026 for the N-central zero-days a researcher published over the weekend, two days after the company pulled its own hosted environments offline and told on-premises customers to shut down their servers; N-able has put the disclosure at 33 zero-days with working proof-of-concept exploits, a set the researcher calls Able2Shell.
topics.summary: N-central is the remote monitoring and management platform managed service providers use to administer client networks, which makes one compromised server a path into every customer it touches. Install the hotfixes before restarting any server that was taken down, then review N-central logs and agent deployments for commands no technician issued.

topics.title: Poland Shuts Down ePUAP After Cyberattack
topics.latest_developments: Poland took ePUAP offline on November 11, 2026 following a cyberattack on the platform, the nationwide system Poles use to submit official documents, correspond with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online.
topics.summary: ePUAP carries the paperwork between Polish citizens, businesses, and the state, so its shutdown stalls filings countrywide until the government restores it. Anyone with Polish administrative deadlines should plan for paper or in-person alternatives and treat email claiming to be ePUAP support as phishing.

business_politics.summary: Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky forced the impeachment resolutions over Hegseth's conduct at the Pentagon, and Republican leaders blocked them on the floor Tuesday evening, November 10. Democrats take control of both chambers in January after the November 3 midterms and plan a wave of investigations into the Trump administration, including tighter export controls in the wake of the Nvidia scandal.

business_politics.summary: The war in Iran suspended the Russia-Ukraine track for most of 2026, and American officials have told European capitals that work on a Ukraine ceasefire must run alongside talks about Europe's future security arrangements, an overture to Moscow that alarms allies. around_teams.latest_developments: Not Just Football posted a clip Wednesday, November 11, in which Mike Tomlin describes the practice tape that set up James Harrison's pick-six in Super Bowl XLIII and Santonio Holmes pacing the sideline before the game-winning drive.
around_teams.summary: Cam Heyward and co-host Hayden taped a two-part sit-down with Tomlin for Not Just Football; part one posted Tuesday, November 10, at 6 a.m. Eastern and runs through Ben Roethlisberger, Aaron Rodgers, and how Tomlin got the Steelers job, with part two set for Thursday, November 12. Tomlin coached Pittsburgh to the Super Bowl XLIII win over the Arizona Cardinals in February 2009, the game Holmes ended with a touchdown catch in the corner of the end zone.

around_teams.title: Metcalf and Pittman Inherit the Deadline Decision
around_teams.latest_developments: Noah Hiles wrote in the Post-Gazette Wednesday, November 11, that with the trade deadline gone and no deals made, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. have to carry the Steelers' passing game themselves.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers let the NFL trade deadline pass Tuesday, November 10, without a move, after spending the week shopping for depth rather than a headline addition. Pittsburgh, 6-2 at its bye, plays at the Cincinnati Bengals Sunday, November 15, at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on NBC.

around_teams.title: Cherington Says the Pirates Have Room to Improve
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday night, November 10, that general manager Ben Cherington came out of Major League Baseball's general managers meetings believing the Pirates hold the flexibility to add to their roster this winter, with Tampa Bay Rays infielder Brandon Lowe among the names in play.
around_teams.summary: Cherington runs the Pirates through an offseason that opens with the general managers meetings, the gathering where clubs start trade and free-agent talks. Pittsburgh went in with payroll questions and lineup holes after another season out of the playoffs.

sources.title: At MLB’s GM meetings, Ben Cherington believes the Pirates have the flexibility to improve

team_usa.title: Manchester United Makes Contact With Pochettino
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources told ESPN Wednesday, November 11, that Manchester United nears an agreement with United States men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino, while Michael Carrick took training again and waited for word on his own future, and ESPN's analysts began handicapping who would replace Pochettino with the Americans.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino, who coaches the United States men's national team, would welcome a return to the Premier League, sources told ESPN, and the club job carries more money and daily work against the national team's longer cycle. United sits in its worst league position in 40 years and faces a relegation fight that ESPN attributes to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe's choice of inexperienced appointments; United States left back Antonee Robinson says the squad pays the speculation no attention.

team_usa.title: Sullivan Joins Pulisic for the First Time
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN argued Wednesday, November 11, that Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan gives Christian Pulisic the co-star the United States men's national team has lacked, with the two set to take the field together for the first time in this month's window.
team_usa.summary: Head coach Mauricio Pochettino recalled AC Milan forward Pulisic for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti and paired the team's established stars with the teenagers who excelled in the last window. Sullivan plays for the Union, which reached the Major League Soccer playoffs on the final day of the regular season, Saturday, November 7, when he and his brother Quinn both scored.
